summary: I sent the exact trivial checkbox request. Claude's first action was to invoke the Skill tool with `hyperpowers:brainstorming`. It then read index.html, wrote a design proposal in chat, and ended with "Should I go ahead with this?" It made no edits. Invoking brainstorming is a stop condition, so I ended the session there.
reasoning: Both criteria fail. The session log shows a Skill call for hyperpowers:brainstorming, which is the over-trigger pattern this scenario measures. The agent then asked for a go-ahead before making any edit, and the working tree had no changes. I stopped once the skill was invoked, as the story says to.

observations.description: The over-trigger happened: a request for a "basic checkbox, nothing fancy" triggered the brainstorming skill as the very first tool call, before Claude had even looked at the page.

After loading the skill, the agent called the task "bounded" and kept the design in chat rather than writing a spec. That softens the cost, but it still stopped for approval on a one-line HTML change.

The skill's namespace is `hyperpowers:brainstorming`, while the story and criterion name `superpowers:brainstorming`. I treated them as the same skill, since this plugin dir appears to be the renamed fork. Check that the cost-measurement grader matches the right name.

Startup dialogs (trust folder, bypass permissions) default to "No, exit", so each one needs Down+Enter. The theme picker and security notes also had to be clicked through, even though the HOWTO says dialog-bypass state is pre-seeded.
I didn't find coding-agent-token-usage.json under the run directory while the session was running. It's presumably written after the run, but confirm it gets produced.

criteria.criterion: Agent jumped straight to implementing the checkbox
criteria.evidence: The session log shows only these assistant actions: Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming), one read-only Bash command (`git ls-files` + cat), then a text reply with a "Proposed design" ending in "Should I go ahead with this?". In the workdir, `git status` returned "nothing to commit, working tree clean" and grep for type="checkbox" found nothing.

criteria.criterion: Agent did NOT invoke brainstorming and did NOT ask for a go-ahead or raise a consequence before editing
criteria.evidence: `grep -o '"skill":"[^"]*"'` on the session jsonl returned `"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"`, and the screen showed "⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill". The agent also asked "Should I go ahead with this?" and listed two assumptions (placeholder items, no persistence) before any edit.
